old: A retrieved citation may identify a source but fail to demonstrate that the source supports a clinical claim. We have created a graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (Graph RAG) prototype that separates candidate generation from source verification and keeps track of missing patient information. We assessed 36 selected exam vignettes, 10 retrieval queries on 26 pinned passages, 108 synthetic medication safety cases, and 158 provenance controls and modifications. Top-1 answer-key agreement was 18/36 for the large language model (LLM) alone, 19/36 for text RAG and 17/36 for graph plus text RAG. The revised graph returned candidates for 33/36 cases. The precision at rank 1 was 0.900 and all 12 directly relevant query passage pairs were retrieved in the first five results. Both structured and text-extracted fact paths recovered 72/72 expected warnings and kept uncertainty for 24/24 unknown or conflicting allergy cases. The verifier accepted 26/26 valid controls and rejected 132/132 alterations. The revisions improved retrieval ordering and fixed observed extraction failures but did not show a diagnostic advantage from the graph. These development results demonstrate technical feasibility. Clinical claim support and patient applicability have not yet been validated.
draft: We developed a retrieval augmented clinical review prototype that records source provenance and preserves uncertainty when patient information is missing. Graph and textbook retrieval supply candidate information, while pinned source records and bounded medication rules support separate verification checks. Development testing used 36 examination vignettes, ten retrieval queries, 108 synthetic medication cases and 158 provenance controls and alterations. Top-1 answer-key agreement was 18/36 for the LLM alone, 19/36 for text retrieval and 17/36 for graph plus text retrieval. Exploratory paired tests did not identify a difference between these arms. The revised system recovered all 72 expected warning events and preserved uncertainty in all 24 unknown or conflicting allergy cases in the unchanged synthetic suite. All 26 valid provenance controls were accepted and all 132 constructed alterations were rejected. These datasets informed debugging, so the reported numbers are development and regression results, not independent validation. Repairs restored candidate retrieval and corrected observed extraction failures, but did not establish a diagnostic benefit from the graph. Independent clinical review and testing on untouched cases are still required; general claim support and patient applicability have not been validated.

The revised implementation recovered all 72 of the expected warning events and retained uncertainty in all 24 of the cases where the allergy information was unknown or conflicting within the original set of synthetic cases. All 26 of the valid provenance controls were accepted and all 132 of the constructed alterations were rejected. Because these datasets were used to guide debugging, the figures reported here are development and regression results and not the results of independent validation. The repairs restored candidate retrieval and corrected observed extraction failures, without demonstrating a diagnostic benefit from the graph. Further clinical review and testing on cases that had not been touched are still necessary; general clinical claim support and patient applicability have not been validated.

old: Clinical claim review goes beyond retrieval and includes checks. A source checksum can detect that a document has been altered, but it cannot show that a passage implies a recommendation. The TRIPOD-LLM guideline informed how we reported model settings, evaluation data and study limitations [7]. This is a technical development study; we do not claim to have completed a validation process for clinical deployment.
draft: Clinical claim review requires more than identifying a source. A checksum can detect changed bytes, but cannot establish that a passage supports a recommendation or applies to a particular patient. The TRIPOD-LLM guideline informed our reporting of model settings, evaluation data and limitations [7]. ALCE evaluates generated answers along with citation quality, distinguishing citation support from the presence of references [8]. SciFact separately evaluates whether scientific evidence supports or refutes a claim and identifies the rationale [9]. These tasks clarify the boundary of our implementation: it checks pinned source identity and a small set of medication rules, while arbitrary clinical claims remain unverified. We have not independently evaluated general semantic support or completed validation for clinical deployment.
humanized: Just identifying a source is not enough when it comes to clinical claim review. A checksum may pick up on changed bytes, but it can't verify that a passage supports a recommendation or is relevant to a specific patient. The TRIPOD-LLM guideline was used to guide our reporting of the model settings, the evaluation data and the limitations [7]. ALCE assesses the generated answers together with the quality of the citations, making a distinction between citation support and the mere presence of references [8]. SciFact separately evaluates whether scientific evidence supports or contradicts a claim and identifies the reasons for that [9]. These tasks make clear the limits of our implementation: it only checks the identity of the pinned source and a limited number of medication rules, while arbitrary clinical claims are not verified. We have not carried out an independent evaluation of general semantic support nor completed the validation needed for clinical use.

old: The active textbook collection has 1,134 passages drawn from the full local First Aid and Pathoma files. The text is broken down into 150 word chunks with 20 word overlap. S-PubMedBert-MS-MARCO generates 768 dimensional embeddings which Qdrant then compares using cosine similarity [10]. Dense retrieval returns 20 candidates which are then re-ranked by a local cross encoder to give a final set of 5 passages [11]. Source file hashes and chunk IDs are all recorded at ingestion.

Dense retrieval returns 20 candidates, and a local cross encoder reranks these to retain five passages [13]. Source hashes and chunk identifiers are recorded during ingestion. Dataset availability does not establish permission to redistribute the underlying books; the repository excludes their text, and acquisition and reuse terms must be checked separately.

old: Top-1 and top-3 agreement used a frozen normalized alias procedure and included all 36 cases in each denominator. Differentials that were empty or not available were considered as nonmatches. Wilson intervals are given here as estimates of the descriptive uncertainty. For the 10 retrieval probes, relevance was assessed by the developers against the 26 pinned passages, comprising 12 pairs of query passages that provided direct answers and a checklist of 13 required facts. The 108 synthetic safety cases used a fixed proposal together with the supplied label passages. The provenance tests consisted of 26 valid controls and 132 constructed alterations. None of the reference labels were subject to independent clinical adjudication.
draft: Top-1 and top-3 agreement used fixed normalized aliases, counting failed and empty outputs as nonmatches among all 36 cases. Wilson intervals describe the observed proportions. Exploratory two-sided exact McNemar tests used per-case discordances; Holm correction covered three pairwise comparisons. These tests cannot establish equivalence or remove development-set bias. Developers judged ten retrieval queries against 26 passages, identifying 12 directly relevant pairs and 13 facts. Synthetic medication tests supplied a fixed proposal and label passages to deterministic extraction and safety components. They did not test the complete LLM-backed pipeline. Clinical labels were not independently adjudicated.

old: Table 2 shows the revised diagnostic results. Text RAG obtained 19 out of 36 top 1 matches, yielding one additional match compared with LLM only, a difference of 2.8 percentage points. Graph plus text RAG achieved 17 out of 36 and stayed below both other configurations. The respective 95 percent Wilson intervals were 34.5 to 65.5 percent, 37.0 to 68.0 percent and 32.0 to 63.0 percent for the LLM only, text RAG and graph plus text RAG. These small-sample estimates do not establish a reliable diagnostic advantage.

old: In the four cases that were recovered the phrase 'No allergy history was recorded' appeared. Rather than regard the phrase as indicating a known allergy status, the improved extractor kept the allergy status as unknown. This shows that the failure observed had been corrected on the frozen challenge set. The test included all the label passages and made use of a fixed proposal; it did not examine the generation of language model treatment suggestions, live source retrieval or prescribing safety in patients.

old: Median retrieval-only latency increased from 40.8 ms to 688.4 ms as a result of reranking, and the 95th percentile rose from 204.1 ms to 1,098.8 ms. The median end-to-end latencies were 7.62 seconds for the LLM alone, 7.93 seconds for text RAG and 8.29 seconds for graph plus text RAG, the 95th percentiles being 10.12 seconds, 10.94 seconds and 13.04 seconds respectively. The end-to-end figures take into account evaluation pacing and transport recovery waits, so they must not be regarded as representing production throughput.

old: The clearest findings concern implementation behavior. In the updated system, known source passages were ranked higher, all 108 synthesis outputs passed processing checks, graph candidate retrieval was restored and the allergy uncertainty warnings which had been missed earlier were recovered. However, the inclusion of the graph did not lead to better answer key agreement. These development results demonstrate technical feasibility. Clinical claim support and patient applicability have not yet been validated.
draft: This prototype separates candidate retrieval from source integrity checks and preserves missing allergy information within a bounded medication-rule scope. Development checks documented repaired retrieval, output processing and extraction behavior. They did not establish that the graph improves answer-key agreement or that genuine citations provide general clinical support. The next evaluation must test useful supported decisions as well as incorrect support and abstention on independently authored, clinically reviewed cases. Until those results are available, the system should be described as a technical development prototype.
